claim: Introduces meta-d' as a metacognitive sensitivity measure and feeds it to a LinUCB/LinTS bandit arbiter for test-time model selection between two image models.
scope_conditions: Image classification (CIFAR-10, PACS+CIFAR-10); CNNs and VLMs; not code, not LLM text
quoted_support: We introduce meta-d', a psychologically-grounded measure of metacognitive sensitivity, to characterise how reliably a model's confidence predicts its own accuracy.

claim: Joint framework gains over best individual model are +7.1% to +8.2% at 300 trials but shrink to 1.4%-3.5% at 1000 trials on CIFAR-10 (Table 1).
stance_target: L3: confidence-routed selection yields modest gains
quoted_support: Table 1 shows that the joint framework's accuracy is significantly improved in the early trials and then stabilises at 1.4%–3.5% higher than that of the individual models.
